A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 11 pages of v1 and 13 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic parameter-estimation experiments, baseline comparisons, initialization tests, and real-world LED and pendulum results.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds results on Delfys75, a loss ablation, and an Euler-step sensitivity study.

M1.justification: The encoder, Euler physics block, and MSE-plus-KL loss remain. V2 Section 5.4 introduces a Torricelli-specific adaptation, changing the KL target prior from N(0,1) to N(1,0.2) to accommodate square-root dynamics.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on Delfys75: real pendulum, draining-water, sliding-block, exponentially decaying LED, and apparent-scale free-fall videos. This substantially expands physical and environmental coverage. V1's linear LED and pendulum examples remain in v2 Appendix A.9, alongside the retained synthetic datasets.

E2.justification: V2 adds an evaluated MSE-only comparator against the full MSE-plus-KL model in Appendix A.4 and Table 3; v1 only discusses its potential collapse. PAIG, NIRPI, and the PAIG-without-U-Net cost comparison remain. Extending the retained baselines to Delfys75 does not itself change their membership.

E3.justification: Delfys75 introduces three settings per system, five videos per setting, individual-video training, a 500-epoch budget for the proposed model, and experiment-specific temporal sampling and batch settings. Separately, the reported synthetic pendulum angle range changes from [-90,90] degrees to [-180,180] degrees; the PDFs do not establish whether that experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a KL-loss ablation testing latent collapse and parameter accuracy (Appendix A.4, Table 3, Figure 9), plus an Euler-step sensitivity study across intensity, Torricelli, and pendulum experiments (Appendix A.8, Table 6). The original initialization-robustness analyses remain.

E5.justification: The original mean-and-standard-deviation reporting over seven initializations is retained. V2 additionally documents ground-truth measurement uncertainty, including instrument resolution and standard deviations calculated across five or fifteen recordings (Appendix A.6, Table 4). Table 2 reports variability across five videos per setting, rather than additional initialization runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive Delfys75 results and both ablation result sets. For example, Table 3 reports oscillator parameters of 3.99 and 0.08 with KL, versus 5.7 and 6.6 with MSE alone. These are newly reported comparisons. The original oscillator estimates survive with equivalent rounding, and the earlier pendulum estimate remains 1.22 m against 1.20 m.

T1.justification: V2 Equation 1 adds an affine constant term to the general ODE formulation. Section 4.1 and Appendix A.6 add physical equations and parameter-calibration derivations. The central Euler and loss derivations remain, with no new theorem or proof. Some added formulas are inconsistent, notably the Torricelli sign across Equations 15 and 23.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion add Delfys75 as a central contribution and claim favorable performance in a structured real-world benchmark. V1 centers its contributions on decoder-free estimation, dynamics beyond motion, extrapolation, and initialization robustness; those claims are retained.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations relating real-world baseline weaknesses to single-video training and spatial-transformer reconstruction, discusses prior rescaling, and identifies Euler-step tradeoffs and sliding-block parameter ambiguity. The principal limitations concerning absolute scale, discretization, interacting-object masks, and autonomous dynamics remain.

D1.justification: V2 provides recording specifications, camera controls, SAM2 mask annotation information, ground-truth measurement procedures, and detailed per-experiment training settings. It also specifies the previously described default initialization more precisely. A concrete code-and-data link and availability statement replace v1's promise of a future GitHub release; external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a dataset discussion positioning Delfys75 against Physics101 and distinguishes the approach from latent-control and equation-learning methods, including NewtonianVAE and LaSDI. Additional citations support annotation and oscillation discussions. The central positioning against PAIG and NIRPI remains.

P1.justification: V2 substantially edits the abstract, introduction, methodological explanations, and discussion. It introduces a dedicated dataset section, consolidates the synthetic experiments, and moves the original real-world examples into the appendix. The author header also changes.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the method diagrams, adds dataset and ablation displays, and extensively reorganizes tables and figures. V1 Table 1 becomes v2 Figure 4b, replacing the separate encoder-versus-ground-truth panel; the cost table is transposed. The original real-world displays move to the appendix, with the LED visualization reformatted.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens two weak points in v1: limited real-world validation and the absence of direct loss-ablation evidence. Delfys75 adds structured comparisons across five physical systems, while the appendices test the KL term and temporal-step sensitivity and document measurement and training procedures. Some new calibration formulas remain internally inconsistent, particularly the Torricelli sign, but these weaknesses do not outweigh the substantial gains in empirical support and reproducibility.
